Sophie (CS): FYI — Acme escalated: embeddings suddenly started returning 1536 dims instead of 1024. Happened right after they rotated keys. Can ENG triage?

Maria (Support): Hmm, do we have a sample request or request_id from them?

Sophie (CS): They sent a curl repro. Shortened: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-202" \
  -H "X-Account-ID: acme-prod" \
  -H "X-Project: acme-web" \
  -d '{"model":"text-embed-small-v1","input":["hello world"]}'
```
They say response dims = 1536. They expect 1024.

Raj (Eng): Do we have logs for that timestamp? if they rotated keys, maybe auth fallback picked an account-level model. Can you paste request_id or an example response header?

Sophie (CS): Request id: req_20250315_9934. Raw response snippet they pasted: 
```
{"model":"text-embed-large-v2","dimensions":1536,"embedding":[...]}
selected_model: text-embed-large-v2
project_id: internal-000
```

Oliver (Infra): Interesting — selected_model != model param. That suggests the router shadowed the requested model with a project/org-level override. @embed-bot can you show routing decision log for req_20250315_9934?

embed-bot: routing-log req_20250315_9934 -> auth: sk-acme-202 (account: acme-prod), headers: X-Project=acme-web, X-Account-ID=acme-prod, effective_project=internal-000, chosen_model=text-embed-large-v2, fallback_reason=project-token-priority.

Lena (SRE): "effective_project=internal-000" stands out. Does the token map to a different project namespace? Could be token->org mapping mismatch after rotation.

Raj (Eng): Another angle — the embeddings path supports micro-batching. If a batch mixes requests from different projects and header precedence logic uses the first subrequest's project, we could accidentally pick the wrong model for the whole batch. Did Acme enable client-side batching?

Sophie (CS): They said yes, they batch 8 inputs per request via our JS SDK with batch:true.

Oliver (Infra): That matches a recent regression we shipped: router used batch-level auth_metadata instead of per-item metadata when X-Project header was present. If a rotated org token belonged to a different default project, the batch got routed to that project's default embedding model.

Maria (Support): Can we reproduce quickly? Steps?

Raj (Eng): Repro steps I used locally:
1) Create two API keys: sk-org-old -> maps to project "internal-000" (default model large-v2), sk-acme-202 -> maps to project "acme-web" (default model small-v1).
2) Send a batched embeddings request with first subrequest using sk-org-old and subsequent subrequests using sk-acme-202 but include X-Project: acme-web on the HTTP header.
3) Observe chosen_model == large-v2 for whole batch.

Command I ran: 
```
# simulate mixed headers in one batch (pseudo)
POST /v1/embeddings
Authorization: Bearer sk-acme-202
X-Project: acme-web
X-Batch-Meta: "first-sub-cred:sk-org-old"
body: {"model":"text-embed-small-v1","input":["a","b","c","d","e"]}
```

Oliver (Infra): Root cause: header precedence + batch-level credential binding. Patch: bind auth metadata at per-item granularity before batching, and ensure X-Project header cannot override token->project mapping unless token is project-scoped.

Lena (SRE): Short-term mitigation for customers: ask them to use project-scoped API keys (psk-*) or include an explicit model override param in the request body: "model":"text-embed-small-v1" — our router should respect explicit model param, but currently the fallback may still overwrite it in edge cases, so prefer project-scoped key.

Raj (Eng): I'll open a hotfix PR to the router: verify token->project mapping is authoritative; do not use X-Project to switch effective project when token is present. Also add unit test for batched mixed-auth.

Oliver (Infra): Rolling the hotfix as a canary to us-west-2 first. Will monitor error rate and embedding dims metric.

Maria (Support): Sophie, please relay workaround to Acme: use their project-scoped key or avoid client-side mixed-tenant batching until we confirm rollout. I'll follow up when hotfix is live. :thumbsup:

Sophie (CS): Sent workaround. They asked if we can retroactively check how many of their calls hit the wrong model — request id list they provided, asked for a timeframe.

Lena (SRE): We can run a log query for acme-prod between 2025-03-15T01:00 and 2025-03-15T03:00 for selected_model!=requested_model and auth_account=acme-prod. I'll run and post counts.

embed-bot: query submitted -> job_7892. Expect results ~5-10 min.

Raj (Eng): Action items: 1) PR + canary (Oliver) 2) Notify CS + provide query results (Lena) 3) Postmortem + changelog entry (Raj).

Sophie (CS): Great, thanks everyone. Will keep Acme updated. :eyes:
